To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
older adults show a deficit in contextual binding.

older participants performed poorer on all task conditions compared to younger adults, with the largest difference between the age groups on the conditions requiring the integration of target and context information.
age-related memory impairment is not equal across memory types, but that especially the integration of multiple episodic features in memory (i.e., binding) is affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of age-related memory decline and the role of contextual memory and binding in this process.
the question of whether age-related memory decline is due to the loss of specific features in memory or to an inability to integrate multiple features in memory.
the question how context memory, binding and episodic memory are interrelated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
older adults are less able to bind information together, especially in situations that require a high level of contextual memory.
the age-related decline in episodic memory is not uniform, and that especially the memory for contextual information and the binding of different features are vulnerable to age-related decline.
the age-related memory decline is not a unitary phenomenon, and that the binding of features in memory is affected to a greater degree than other aspects of episodic memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of features in memory, especially the binding of context information to a target, is a crucial component of memory that is particularly affected in older adults.
the older adults are less able to remember the context of the target and to bind target-context and context-context information.
older adults are less able to bind contextual features to target features and are also less able to bind two contextual features to one another.
The main takeaway from our work is that
older adults have a more difficult time remembering where they saw something or when they saw it compared to younger adults.
the ability to integrate multiple features in a memory trace is more affected by aging than the ability to store and recall a single feature.
the ability to bind together different features of an event is affected in older adults.
